note: Re-judged 2026-11-24 (independent reader) against RFC 9252 Section 2: 'If the BGP next hop is unchanged during the advertisement, the SRv6 Service TLVs, including any unrecognized Types of Sub-TLV and Sub-Sub-TLV, SHOULD be propagated further. In addition, all Reserved fields in the TLV, Sub-TLV, or Sub-Sub-TLV MUST be propagated unchanged.' applyEgressPrefixSIDNextHop compares the original received next-hop entity against the final effective emitted entity (after policy, configured rewrite, and link-local scope normalization) on both cached and RS forward rails, leaving attribute 40 untouched when equal. TestRFC9252EffectiveNextHopControlsServiceTLVs (now strengthened with NextHopAuto connected-endpoint rewriting, auto-already-self, and auto-policy-change-restored-to-self controls), TestPrefixSIDPropagationNextHop, and TestRFC9252ReservedFieldsPropagatedUnchanged inspect actual recipient wire output and assert byte-identical L3/L2 Service TLVs including non-zero Reserved octets (TLV RESERVED 0xA5, Sub-TLV Reserved1 0x5A, Reserved2 0xC3) and unrecognized Sub-TLV 0xF0 / Sub-Sub-TLV 0xEE when unchanged, paired with changed-next-hop counter-controls that strip Service TLVs. Verdict remains enforced.
